content: @Query auto-updates on insert/delete/change; onAppear is documented as too late for state setup (view body already committed) and Apple recommends .task over onAppear-driven refetch. iOS 18.0/18.1 had regressions where SwiftData did not surface updates from background ModelActors. No official guidance on suppressing a visible refetch during a transition -- must be handled at the view layer (e.g. snapshot/freeze content during animation).
